Calculate Neighbourhood Clonal Diversity Indices

Source: R/nhood_diversity.R
nhood_diversity.Rd

Computes diversity metrics for each neighbourhood in a Milo or SingleCellExperiment object, using clonal identifiers (clone IDs or CDR3 sequences) extracted from colData.

Usage

nhood_diversity(
  object,
  nhood_col = NULL,
  clone_id_col = NULL,
  cdr3_col = "cdr3_aa_VDJ",
  min_n_contigs = 20,
  metrics = c("shannon", "inv.simpson", "gini.simpson", "chao1"),
  downsample_method = "rarefaction",
  n_boots = 100,
  feature_scale = FALSE,
  result_name = "nhood_diversity"
)

Arguments

object

A Milo or SingleCellExperiment object. Seurat objects must first be converted via as.SingleCellExperiment.

nhood_col

Character string. For plain SingleCellExperiment objects (i.e. not Milo), the name of the colData column containing neighbourhood assignments. Not required for Milo objects.

clone_id_col

Character string. Name of the colData column containing clone identifiers. If NULL or not found, cdr3_col is used as a fallback.

cdr3_col

Character string. Name of the colData column containing CDR3 amino-acid sequences. Used when clone_id_col is unavailable. Default: "cdr3_aa_VDJ".

min_n_contigs

Integer. Minimum number of cells with contig availability required for a neighbourhood to be considered reliable. Neighbourhoods below this threshold are flagged with diversity_reliable = FALSE and their metric values are set to NA. Default: 20.

metrics

Character vector of diversity metrics to compute. Any combination of "shannon", "norm.entropy", "inv.simpson", "gini.simpson", "chao1", "ace", "gini" and "standardised_n_clones". "standardised_n_clones" computes coverage-standardised observed clone richness via iNEXT::estimateD with Hill number order \(q = 0\) and can only be requested if downsample_method = "coverage". Default: c("shannon", "inv.simpson", "gini.simpson", "chao1").

downsample_method

Character string specifying how to standardise sequencing depth across neighbourhoods before computing metrics. One of:

"rarefaction"

Random subsampling to the median contig count across valid neighbourhoods (base R implementation). The rarefaction depth is reported at runtime. Neighbourhoods whose contig count is at or below the rarefaction depth are not downsampled; this can occur frequently when neighbourhood sizes vary widely. Rarefaction is preferred when communities are highly diverse or singleton- dominated, as it standardises sample size rather than coverage. "chao1" and "ace" are not rarefied; they are computed on observed counts and <metric>_diversity_sd is NA for these metrics.

"vegan_rarefaction"

As above, using vegan::rrarefy. Requires the vegan package. The same guidance on rarefaction depth interpretation and "chao1"/ "ace" compatibility applies.

"coverage"

Coverage-based standardisation via iNEXT::estimateD. Requires the iNEXT package. The target coverage is set to the median Good's coverage (\(1 - singletons / n\)) across valid neighbourhoods and is reported at runtime. Coverage-based standardisation is preferred when neighbourhood sizes are large and relatively uniform. If the reported target coverage is very low (near 0), rarefaction may be more appropriate. "chao1", "ace", "norm.entropy", and "gini" are not coverage standardised; they are computed on observed counts and <metric>_diversity_se is NA for these metrics.

"none"

No downsampling; metrics are computed on the observed counts directly. No spread columns are added to the output.

Default: "rarefaction".

n_boots

Integer. Number of bootstrap replicates used when downsample_method is "rarefaction" or "vegan_rarefaction". Default: 100. For reproducible results, call set.seed() before invoking this function.

feature_scale

Logical. If TRUE, a min-max scaled version of each diversity metric (range 0-1) is appended to the output as <metric>_diversity_scaled. Default: FALSE.

result_name

Character string. Key under which the results data.frame is stored in metadata(object). Default: "nhood_diversity".

Value

The input object, with a data.frame of diversity results stored in metadata(object)[[result_name]]. The data.frame contains the following columns:

nhood

Neighbourhood identifier.

nhood_size

Total number of cells in the neighbourhood.

n_contigs

Number of cells with a contig.

contig_capture_rate

Fraction of cells with a contig (n_contigs / nhood_size).

n_clones

Observed number of unique clones.

clone_per_contig

Ratio of unique clones to cells with a valid contig (n_clones / n_contigs). Values near 1 indicate high clonal diversity; values near 0 indicate strong clonal expansion.

coverage

Good's coverage estimate (\(1 - singletons / n\)).

diversity_reliable

Logical; TRUE if n_contigs >= min_n_contigs.

<metric>_diversity

Estimated diversity for each requested metric.

<metric>_diversity_sd

Standard deviation of the metric across bootstrap iterations. Present only when downsample_method is "rarefaction" or "vegan_rarefaction". NA for "chao1" and "ace", which are not bootstrapped.

<metric>_diversity_se

Analytical standard error derived from iNEXT confidence intervals. Present only when downsample_method = "coverage". NA for "chao1", "ace", "norm.entropy", and "gini", which are not coverage-standardised.

<metric>_diversity_scaled

Min-max scaled diversity (only present when feature_scale = TRUE).

The following attributes are also set on the returned data.frame: min_n_contigs and method are always present. rarefy_depth is set only when downsample_method is "rarefaction" or "vegan_rarefaction". target_coverage is set only when downsample_method is "coverage".

Details

Object type handling

  • Milo objects: Neighbourhood membership is read directly from the sparse nhoods matrix via nhoods. Row names of this matrix must match colnames(object); a mismatch raises an error to prevent silent misassignment.

  • Plain SingleCellExperiment objects: A binary neighbourhood membership matrix is constructed internally from the column specified by nhood_col. Cells with NA assignments are excluded with a warning.

Clone identity resolution

clone_id_col is tried first; if it is NULL or absent from colData, the function falls back to cdr3_col with a warning. Cells whose clone/CDR3 value is NA, "", "No_contig", or "None" are excluded from diversity calculations but are still counted in nhood_size.

Metric selection

The bias-corrected Chao1 formula (\(S_{obs} + F_1(F_1-1) / (2(F_2+1))\)) is used rather than the classicformula (\(S_{obs} + F_1^2 / (2 F_2)\)).

Downsampling and metric compatibility

Rarefaction ("rarefaction" and "vegan_rarefaction") is not applied to "chao1" or "ace", as subsampling removes the singleton and doubleton structure these estimators rely on. Both are always computed on observed counts under rarefaction; _diversity_sd is NA for these metrics.

Under "coverage", only "shannon", "inv.simpson", "gini.simpson", and "standardised_n_clones" are coverage-standardised via iNEXT. "chao1", "ace", "norm.entropy", and "gini" fall back to observed-count calculation with a runtime warning; _diversity_se is NA for these metrics.

"standardised_n_clones" is only valid with downsample_method = "coverage"; requesting it under any other method raises an error.

Reproducibility

Bootstrap-based methods ("rarefaction", "vegan_rarefaction") use base::sample internally. For reproducible results, call set.seed() before invoking this function.

Note

The vegan package is required when downsample_method = "vegan_rarefaction" and iNEXT is required when downsample_method = "coverage".

See also

nhood_shm, nhood_cdr3_convergence, nhood_annotation, nhood_annotation_props

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# --- Milo object, default metrics and rarefaction -------------------------
milo <- nhood_diversity(
  object       = milo_object,
  clone_id_col = "clone_id",
  cdr3_col     = "cdr3_aa_VDJ"
)
results <- S4Vectors::metadata(milo)[["nhood_diversity"]]

# --- Coverage standardisation with standardised_n_clones ----------------
milo <- nhood_diversity(
  object            = milo_object,
  clone_id_col      = "clone_id",
  metrics           = c("shannon", "inv.simpson", "gini.simpson",
                        "standardised_n_clones"),
  downsample_method = "coverage",
  feature_scale     = TRUE,
  result_name       = "nhood_diversity_coverage"
)

# --- Plain SingleCellExperiment object ------------------------------------
sce <- nhood_diversity(
  object       = sce_object,
  clone_id_col = "clone_id",
  nhood_col    = "neighbourhood_id"
)
} # }
